label: copy-phase input p (fed-back copy of p) in long sequences
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps). It fires only in the copy phase, never on original-phase or <DEL> steps, and only on later copy steps (recall_idx >= 3, t >= 10). It is concentrated in long sequences: L=9 holds 89% of the mass and L=8 holds 10%. About 78% of the mass is on steps where the fed-back input is p. The remainder is mostly on inputs j, r and 2. The largest activations are p fed back at recall_idx 5-8, usually with the final or near-final token being output next (s, j, h, digits). Its rate rises steeply toward the last step of a 9-token sequence (25x lift at t=17). Precision is poor: only about 4% of late copy-phase p inputs in long sequences cross the threshold, and I found no simple history variable (out_tok, prev tokens, first token) that separates the active cases. So this is a sparse tail of some distributed quantity, not a clean detector. Using {p,j,r,2} as inputs raises mass recall to 0.96 but cuts precision to about 1%.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=p (+5.60), phase=2 & in_tok=j (+3.07), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+2.75), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+2.65), phase=2 & out_tok=j (+2.32), phase=2 & out_tok=s (+2.13). Lower it: orig7=- (-2.53), recall_idx=1 (-1.89), prev_tok=<DEL> (-1.89), orig8=- (-1.76).
